creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`format_epoch`, `get_os`, `mkdir` and the path helpers landed in `f69ebced` (2026-07-08), after the v0.11.0 tag. The review machine ran that untagged dev build, so its "available now" notes don't map cleanly onto the release.

Three main-board cards look like candidates for already-done: "Epoch-to-string date formatting (inverse of parse_date)", "RAD-182: add functions for adding days, etc to time", and the untriaged "date parsing functionality". Check before scheduling any of them.

The review also lists workarounds in live scripts that expired when their fixes landed: `remind:136-140`, `work:407`, `progressions:64`, `valstate:54`, `htree:190-193`, `vers:41`, `kwatch:34-40`. Their comments now describe problems that no longer exist. Nothing tells an author their workaround expired, which is worth a thought of its own.

---

### Premise, verified

Checked 2026-08-10 against `/Users/amterp/src/rad` on `main`. Everything the card asserts holds:

- Commit `f69ebced3e6a2d06e3f774ee6d089c1bcae8cfa1`, dated **2026-07-08**: `feat: add get_os, mkdir, path helpers, and format_epoch builtins`.
- Tag `v0.11.0` points at a commit dated **2026-07-03**. So `f69ebced` landed five days *after* the release. The card's core claim - that the review machine ran an untagged dev build - is correct, and `v0.11.0` is still the newest tag (`git tag --sort=-creatordate | head -1`).
- `f69ebced` added six builtins, not four: `base_name`, `dir_name`, `format_epoch`, `get_os`, `join_paths`, `mkdir`. Docs for all six are in `docs/funcs/`.

Date/time surface on `main` today, from `docs/funcs/`: `format_epoch`, `now`, `parse_date`, `parse_epoch`. That is the full inventory to compare the three candidate cards against.

The three candidate cards, located on the `main` board:

| Card | Column | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `a_1WDM0KVaL` | `high` | Epoch-to-string date formatting (inverse of parse_date) |
| `3d86xlf9` | `high` | RAD-182: add functions for adding days, etc to time |
| `a_m0vosQ81` | *(none)* | date parsing functionality |

`a_m0vosQ81` has no column at all, which matches the card's "untriaged". Note there is also `a_1WDM0AQVj` "Time maps: add day-of-week field", already in `done` - useful as a reference for what a resolved one looks like.

### How to run the check

```sh
cd /Users/amterp/src/rad
make build          # bin/radd. A bare `rad` is the installed release - it will answer for v0.11.0, which is the wrong build.
```

For each of the three cards, read what it actually asks for, then check it against the current build:

```sh
kan show a_1WDM0KVaL -b main
./bin/radd docs format_epoch
./bin/radd docs parse_date
```

`rad docs <func>` renders the same Markdown that lives in `docs/funcs/<name>.md`, which is the type checker's source of truth - so the signature it prints is authoritative, not a mirror that might be stale.

Then prove it end to end with a scratch script in a temp dir:

```sh
D=$(mktemp -d)
cat > $D/probe.rad <<'EOF'
<snippet exercising exactly what the card asks for>
EOF
./bin/radd $D/probe.rad
```

Read `SYNTAX.md` before writing the snippet.

### What pass and fail look like

Three outcomes, and the middle one is the trap:

- **Fully shipped** - a function exists whose signature and behavior cover everything the card asks for. Move the card to `done` on the `main` board with a one-line note naming `f69ebced` and the function.
- **Partially shipped** - a function exists but does less than the card asks. This is the likely outcome for `RAD-182` (adding days to a time), since `format_epoch` and `parse_epoch` convert but do not do arithmetic. Do **not** close these. Edit the card down to only the remaining gap, and say which part landed and where.
- **Not shipped** - leave it alone, and note on the card that you checked at commit `<sha>` so the next person does not repeat the work.

A signature existing is not proof the card is done. Run the snippet.

### Where the answers go

- The three cards above, on the **`main`** board (`kan edit <id> -b main -d "..."`, never `-f`, which would clobber labels).
- Append a short results summary to this card so the sprint board carries the outcome too.

### The expired-workarounds half

The card's second paragraph lists live scripts whose workaround comments are now obsolete: `remind:136-140`, `work:407`, `progressions:64`, `valstate:54`, `htree:190-193`, `vers:41`, `kwatch:34-40`.

**Those scripts are not in this repo.** They live in the user's own scripts repo. Do not go hunting for them here. This half of the card is the user's to action, not an agent's - unless the user points you at that repo explicitly.

The generalizable observation is the interesting part and it does belong to this repo: nothing tells a script author that the workaround they wrote has expired. If that turns into a feature idea - a lint, or something in `rad check`, or a note in the release notes - raise it as its own card rather than growing this one.
title: Confirm which high-priority main-board cards already shipped
